text: For more than 40 years, Inglewood has been my home. It is where I was raised, built my business, raised my family, and dedicated my life to serving our community.

For the past eight years, I have proudly served as an Inglewood Housing Commissioner, advocating for residents and protecting affordable housing opportunities. As a small business owner for over 10 years co-founder of the Taste of Inglewood, and community leader, I have worked to strengthen our local economy, created opportunities for entrepreneurs, and brought our neighborhoods together through service and civic engagement.
My campaign is built on accountability, transparency, visibility, and compassion. I believe residents deserve a Councilmember who listens, is accessible, and puts people before politics.

I understand the challenges facing District 1, from public safety and housing affordability to supporting small businesses, improving city services, and investing in our youth. I am committed to practical solutions that protect our neighborhoods while creating opportunities for future generations.
I respectfully ask for your vote for Inglewood City Council, District 1, so together we can build a stronger, safer, and more united Inglewood.

text: My name is Leonard Redway, and as a current District 1 Commissioner, longtime Inglewood resident, community advocate, single parent, and business owner, I am prepared to represent your voice at City Hall.

I have firsthand experience, professional training, and a deep commitment to addressing the issues that matter most to our residents. As your Councilmember, my priorities will include improving public safety in our District, reducing crime, easing traffic congestion, adjusting parking permitting, limiting excessive billboards, and ensuring residents receive reliable city services.

We should not have to sit in overwhelming traffic just to get home. Our neighborhoods should be safe, clean, and protected. City government should be transparent, accountable, and responsive to the people it serves.

As a Director of Facilities and Public Safety at a cultural institution, I manage safety operations, emergency response, facilities, construction projects, and essential services. That experience has prepared me to advocate for safer communities and better management of city resources.
Please vote Leonard Redway for Inglewood City Council, District 1.

text: Age: 53
Occupation: Business Owner

I am a wife, mother, and lifelong resident of Inglewood. I have witnessed the city's triumphs and challenges and have remained steadfast in my commitment to Inglewood. I have stood with families seeking answers, organized residents, and ensured their voices are heard. Representation means being present, accessible, and willing to listen, not only during election season. Inglewood deserves leadership focused on improving residents' quality of life. Safety, accountability, transparency, and the use of taxpayer dollars must be priorities. I will work to address the traffic issues that plague our district, advocate for cleaner air and to reduce aviation noise, support our seniors and local businesses, and promote responsible development that benefits residents.

I believe Inglewood is at its best when we work together. Our progress should strengthen neighborhoods, create opportunities, and ensure that everyone wins, not just corporations and special interests.

I will bring independent leadership, common sense, compassion, and a community voice to City Hall. I respectfully ask for your vote and the opportunity to serve District 1 while continuing to fight for the Soul of Inglewood.

text: Occupation: Business Owner

For 16 years I've run my own business in Inglewood meeting budgets managing resources and delivering results for my customers and my community. That hands on experience shapes how our city spends money and sets rates.

As Vice chair of Inglewood Unified's Asset Management Committee, I help oversee how public resources are managed for our students and families. As a member of GPAC/Next Level Inglewood, I work directly with residents on the issues that matter most.
I've called Inglewood home for over 20 years, and I've watched neighbors squeezed by rising utility costs, worsening traffic, and an affordability crisis pushing longtime residents out.
Elected to represent District 1, I'll bring my real-world experience to fight for fairer utility pricing, real traffic solutions, and an Inglewood we can still afford to call home.
